findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing anonymous or unauthorized users to read/write objects including sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (including the sensitive customer-master file) cannot be recovered, increasing risk of data loss/tampering.
A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science bucket contents are stored unencrypted at rest.
